t: Stereo Vision Processor - Signature build-tool concept
title: Stereo Vision Processor - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Estimates depth using compatible stereo-image inputs.
description:
Stereo Vision Processor is the Signature build-tool concept that estimates depth using compatible stereo-image inputs. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Stereo Vision Processor the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Stereo Vision Processor will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Convolver - Stereo Vision Processor framework pillar
title: Signature Convolver - Stereo Vision Processor framework pillar
definition: The Convolver component of the Signature Stereo Vision Processor framework, owning convolver. Signature concept.
description:
The Convolver is a load-bearing component of the Signature Stereo Vision Processor framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's convolver responsibilities belongs to the Convolver, and the Convolver answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Convolver can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Convolver works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Stereo Vision Processor charter (estimates depth using compatible stereo-image inputs.). The Convolver reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small vision job that needs Stereo Vision Processor. The Convolver takes the request's convolver responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Convolver's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Stereo Vision Processor. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Augmenter - Stereo Vision Processor framework pillar
title: Signature Augmenter - Stereo Vision Processor framework pillar
definition: The Augmenter component of the Signature Stereo Vision Processor framework, owning augmenter. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Stereo Vision Processor framework, the Augmenter owns the framework's augmenter responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Augmenter's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Augmenter from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Estimates depth using compatible stereo-image inputs.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Computer vision and visual understanding build needs Stereo Vision Processor, so the framework invokes the Augmenter on the the framework's augmenter responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Suppressor - Stereo Vision Processor framework pillar
title: Signature Suppressor - Stereo Vision Processor framework pillar
definition: The Suppressor component of the Signature Stereo Vision Processor framework, owning suppressor. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Stereo Vision Processor framework decomposes the capability (Estimates depth using compatible stereo-image inputs.) into seven pillars, and the Suppressor is the one that owns the framework's suppressor responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Stereo Vision Processor result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Suppressor's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Suppressor's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Stereo Vision Processor. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.
